subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: What security boundary should OpenClaw officially support for agent-usable secrets that must be usable by tools but not visible to the agent?
rationale: The evidence shows partial SecretRef and hook mitigation, but the remaining behavior defines a credential trust boundary and user-facing guarantee that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Sponsor a core/secops design
options.body: Define a native credential injection and redaction boundary, including config/API shape, migration/audit behavior, exec semantics, and plugin-provider extension points before implementation.

options.title: Defer to plugins and OS isolation
options.body: Document the current SecretRef plus plugin-hook plus OS/container isolation model as the supported approach and keep core from promising arbitrary masked command secrets.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Explicitly reject native masked secrets in core and direct users to external credential proxies or ClawHub plugins for this threat model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core/secops design
recommendation.body: Define a native credential injection and redaction boundary, including config/API shape, migration/audit behavior, exec semantics, and plugin-provider extension points before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The central files and docs are CODEOWNERS-routed to this security owner team, and the requested behavior is a credential boundary decision.
